title: Heritage walk in Hyderabad: Charminar, Golconda and the Qutb Shahi tombs
seo_title: Heritage Walk in Hyderabad: Historical Places and Routes
meta_description: Plan a heritage walk in Hyderabad: Charminar, Chowmahalla, Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs, museums and walking routes for schools and groups.
summary: A heritage walk in Hyderabad covers two connected landscapes: Golconda Fort and the Qutb Shahi tombs, the seat of the Qutb Shahi sultans from the early 16th century; and the old city around the Charminar (1591), with Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace and the Laad Bazaar. A vehicle is needed between the two, which lie about 10 km apart.

sections.h2: Why Hyderabad matters for Indian heritage
paras: Hyderabad is one of the best places in India to study a Deccani sultanate capital and the court culture that followed it. The Qutb Shahi dynasty ruled from Golconda from about 1518 until the Mughal conquest of 1687. In 1591 Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded a new planned city on the Musi river, with the Charminar at its centre. In the 18th century the Asaf Jahi Nizams made Hyderabad the capital of the largest princely state in India, which joined the Indian Union in 1948.

Each phase left buildings that can be read on foot: a hill fort with water systems, a royal necropolis, a planned grid of bazaars and palaces from the Nizams' time. Our explainer on [Indo-Islamic architecture](indo-islamic-architecture.html) gives the vocabulary of domes, arches and minarets you will use on the walk.

sections.h2: Historical places in Hyderabad by period
paras: Golconda began as a Kakatiya mud fort, probably in the 12th or 13th century, before it passed to the Bahmanis and then to Sultan Quli, founder of the Qutb Shahi line. The Qutb Shahi tombs west of the fort hold the graves of seven sultans and members of their families, set in a garden that the Aga Khan Trust for Culture and the Telangana government have conserved over the last decade.

The old city is a 16th and 17th century plan with later layers. The Charminar was followed by Mecca Masjid, begun in 1617 and finished under Aurangzeb in 1694. The Nizams built Chowmahalla Palace in the 18th and 19th centuries and Falaknuma Palace in 1893. The British Residency at Koti (1803 to 1806) marks the colonial relationship.

sections.h2: What you see on a heritage walk in Hyderabad
paras: At Golconda the walk climbs from the Fateh Darwaza through the Bala Hisar gate, where a hand clap under the dome carries to the top of the hill, a feature guides demonstrate for every group. Along the way look for the water lifts, cisterns and the granaries that let the fort hold out against the Mughal siege of 1687 for about eight months. The Qutb Shahi tombs nearby show square tombs on high plinths with onion domes, a distinctly Deccani design.

In the old city, start at the Charminar and look at the four arches aligned on the main streets, then walk to Mecca Masjid, the Laad Bazaar for lacquer bangles and Chowmahalla Palace. The [Deccan temple forms lecture](deccan-temple-forms-vesara-debates.html) is not about mosques, but it helps older students see that the Deccan developed its own building traditions over many centuries.

The Salar Jung Museum holds a very large private collection gathered mostly by Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III, including the Veiled Rebecca marble, jade, manuscripts and clocks. The Telangana State Archaeology Museum at Public Gardens has Buddhist sculpture from sites in the Krishna valley and an Egyptian mummy. A [museum gallery study with an archaeologist](museum-morning-with-an-archaeologist.html) helps groups focus on a few strong objects rather than walking past thousands.

sections.h2: Hyderabad heritage walk for schools and colleges
paras: For schools, Golconda works best early in the morning: it is open ground, the acoustics trick delights younger students, and it ties to the Deccan sultanates in the medieval India syllabus. Colleges can take on the full old city walk and the conservation questions at the Qutb Shahi tombs, where restoration has been extensive and well documented.

We arrange Hyderabad walks to suit your group and its interests. Groups travelling further can add Warangal and the Ramappa Temple through a [study tour built for your group](a-study-tour-built-for-your-group.html), or a [heritage photography walk](heritage-photography-evidence-led-photo-walk.html) in the old city for media and design students.

The old city is crowded from late morning, especially near the Charminar and in Ramzan evenings. Start early, keep groups small and agree a meeting point. Mosques have their own visiting rules and prayer timings. Golconda has a long uphill climb with uneven steps. Check the ASI, museum or site website for current timings before you go.
Use a hired vehicle between Golconda and the old city. For the wider region, see [heritage sites in Telangana](heritage-sites-in-telangana.html).

stops.name: Golconda Fort
stops.note: Hill fortress with outer walls, gates, cisterns and granaries. Try the hand clap at the Fateh Darwaza portico.

stops.name: Bala Hisar
stops.note: The summit of Golconda with the durbar hall and a view over the city. A steep climb of several hundred steps.

stops.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
stops.note: Royal necropolis of the Qutb Shahi sultans. Compare the tombs' plinths, domes and stucco work.

stops.name: Toli Masjid
stops.note: A small Qutb Shahi mosque on the road between Golconda and the old city, known for its fine stucco.

stops.name: Charminar
stops.note: Four-arched monument at the crossing of the old city's main streets. Look at the minarets and the mosque on the upper floor.

stops.name: Mecca Masjid
stops.note: One of the largest mosques in India, finished under Aurangzeb. The Asaf Jahi tombs lie in an enclosure beside it.

stops.name: Laad Bazaar
stops.note: Lane of lacquer bangle makers leading from the Charminar. A good place to talk about craft and trade.

stops.name: Chowmahalla Palace
stops.note: Seat of the Nizams with four palaces around courtyards. The Khilwat durbar hall and vintage cars are highlights.

stops.name: Purani Haveli
stops.note: A Nizam's palace with a long wing now holding the Nizam's Museum.

stops.name: Salar Jung Museum
stops.note: A huge collection from three generations of Salar Jungs. Choose a few galleries rather than trying to see all.

stops.name: British Residency
stops.note: Neoclassical residence of the British Resident, now part of a women's college. Visits need permission.

stops.name: Falaknuma Palace
stops.note: Hilltop palace in a European style, now a hotel. Usually seen from outside.

routes.name: Golconda and the royal tombs
routes.length: About 3.5 hours, short drive between fort and tombs

museums.name: Salar Jung Museum
museums.note: Indian, European and East Asian art collected by the Salar Jung family.

museums.name: Telangana State Archaeology Museum
museums.note: Buddhist sculpture, prehistoric tools and coins at Public Gardens, Nampally.

museums.name: Nizam's Museum, Purani Haveli
museums.note: Gifts and objects associated with the last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan.

best_time: October to February, when days are dry and mornings cool. Summer afternoons on Golconda are very hot.

faq.q: What are the main historical places in Hyderabad?
faq.a: Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs, the Charminar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, Purani Haveli, the Salar Jung Museum and the British Residency. Golconda and the old city are about 10 km apart.
The Charminar was built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah when he founded the new city of Hyderabad. It stands at the crossing of the main streets of the planned city.

faq.q: How much time do I need at Golconda Fort?
faq.a: Allow two to three hours to walk from the gate to the Bala Hisar and back, with time for the water systems and the hand clap at the entrance. Add an hour for the Qutb Shahi tombs.

faq.q: Is a Hyderabad heritage walk suitable for schools?
faq.a: Yes. Golconda is open and good for younger students in the early morning. The old city is crowded, so it suits smaller groups of older students with one adult for every ten or so students.

faq.q: Is Golconda a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faq.a: Not yet. The Qutb Shahi monuments of Hyderabad, including Golconda and the Charminar, are on India's Tentative List. In Telangana the inscribed site is the Ramappa Temple, near Warangal.

posts.hook: Golconda held out against the Mughals for about eight months.
posts.caption: Its cisterns, water lifts and granaries let the fort survive the siege of 1687. Look for them on the climb to the Bala Hisar.

posts.hook: Stand under the Charminar and look down the four streets.
posts.caption: Each arch lines up with a main road of the 1591 city plan. The monument was the centre of a designed grid, not a lone gate.
